critical_evidence.evidence: No borescope mentioned. The 'Inspection / Service' entry (07/2025) does not say a borescope was performed.
No IMS retrofit and no engine number stated. On a 2005 M96 the original bearing is likely the higher-risk single-row type unless retrofitted.
Oil changes are claimed at 89k and about 91k, but no filter-media inspection is mentioned.
No fault memory or cam deviation data provided.
The car is pictured only with the hardtop on. The soft top, drains and footwell dryness are not examined here.

documentation.rationale: The VIN is given and decodes cleanly. The listing also has an itemised, dated maintenance log and voluntarily discloses flaws, including a Carfax damage event. However, there are no receipts, no Carfax copy, no engine number or IMS evidence, and no photos of the at-risk areas. That is the identity half plus a prose log, without the proof half.

condition.rationale: The photos show a tidy exterior and frunk and a manual interior with moderate seat-leather wear. No fault is stated. Disclosed paint chips are minor. Engine health is entirely unproven: no borescope, no scan, no cooling or IMS history. The AOS and engine-mount work are claimed only.

price_value.rationale: The $23,000 ask is roughly 55% above the $14,817 fair value midpoint. The comps are thin and from 2006, but a 2006 Boxster S at 93k sold for $13,100. The 2005 carries open IMS risk with no retrofit, so the options, manual and hardtop do not close the gap.

mission_fit.rationale: It is a manual S with Sport Chrono, which suits a keeper. But it is the highest-IMS-risk model year with no retrofit or borescope evidence, and it is priced well above comps. That is not the documented superiority a keeper premium requires, and it conflicts with cash preservation.

logistics.rationale: Tucson is a fly-and-drive trip with Porsche specialists nearby, and private-party terms are simple. PPI access is not stated. CA smog should be feasible.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: Several desirable traits: 6-speed manual, S model, Sport Chrono Plus, OEM hardtop, and an unusual claimed colour (Dark Olive) over Sand Beige. These are offset by gold aftermarket wheels and gold-painted grilles, which are a taste-specific departure from stock.

evidence.mission_note: As a future keeper it offers the right ingredients (manual, S, Sport Chrono, hardtop). However, it is the highest-IMS-risk 987.1 year with no IMS or bore evidence, priced well above comps, so it conflicts with the current cash-preservation strategy unless documentation proves superiority.
evidence.rationale: The listing establishes a VIN-confirmed 2005 Boxster S. Photos confirm the 6-speed manual, Sport Chrono dash pod, OEM hardtop, and aftermarket gold wheels and grilles. The seller provides a dated maintenance log (AOS 01/2025, engine mounts 11/2024, coolant and brake fluid 08/2026) and discloses a Carfax damage event attributed to a shopping cart, but none of it is backed by receipts or a report. The model-critical evidence is entirely absent: no engine number or IMS documentation on a 2005 M96, no borescope, no scan data, no filter cut, no cooling-component receipts, and no soft-top evidence. Observed issues are minor paint chips and the undocumented damage event. The $23,000 ask sits well above the $14,817 fair value midpoint drawn from thin 2006 comps. Tire dates, clutch history and owner count remain open.
evidence.next_action: Message the seller for the engine number, any IMS invoice, the Carfax report and receipts for the listed work, and ask whether a Tucson Porsche specialist can do a borescope PPI before any deposit.
